title: correlation_id plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `correlation_id` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component CorrelationIdConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

CorrelationIdConfig.description: Plugin: correlation_id — With the default inbound_policy preserve, keeps a non-empty inbound ID only when it is at most 256 bytes and matches [A-Za-z0-9._-]+; every missing or rejected value is replaced (never truncated) with UUID v4. With inbound_policy generate, every HTTP/gRPC/WebSocket request receives a fresh gateway-owned UUID v4 that overwrites any inbound value on that header. Multiple instances retain independent authoritative values in private typed request/session state. The first instance in priority order owns the canonical request_id, while every instance forwards and echoes only its own private value, including on successful H1/H2/H3 WebSocket handshakes. Public request_id and correlation_id.instance.* metadata are compatibility projections; later plugin writes cannot change authoritative forwarding, echo, or logged values. Effective instances on one proxy chain that overlap on any supported protocol must normalize to distinct header_name values and have distinct effective priorities; use priority_override to make canonical ownership deterministic. Disjoint protocol owners do not conflict. Admission and reload reject either overlapping ambiguous composition. Runtime admission also rejects the deployment-specific effective FERRUM_REAL_IP_HEADER value case-insensitively; that dynamic exclusion cannot be expressed by this static schema. CP/DP config sync requires every DP to advertise the same effective value as the CP before configuration is distributed. The top-level config must be an object; null fields select defaults.

header_name.description: Header name (surrounding Rust `str::trim` Unicode White_Space is trimmed and the name is lowercased internally). After trimming, the token must be a valid `http::HeaderName` of at most 65,535 ASCII bytes. Used for the inbound preserved value and this instance's outbound/echoed value. Protocol-managed request, forwarding, framing, connection, content-coding, W3C tracing context (traceparent and tracestate), gRPC status, WebSocket handshake, and internal marker names (including early-data, x-grpc-web-mode, and x-ferrum-original-content-encoding), plus security-sensitive credential/authentication names, every name in the gateway-owned x-consumer-* consumer assertion namespace (with `_` equivalent to `-`, so x_consumer_role is included), the other gateway-owned backend assertions that outbound refresh strips and regenerates (x-authenticated-identity and the GeoIP x-geo-country, either spelling), the literal x-real-ip that backend builders drop from untrusted peers, and the gateway-owned x-ferrum-hops proxy hop count (either spelling), are rejected case-insensitively. Runtime also rejects the effective deployment-specific FERRUM_REAL_IP_HEADER value case-insensitively; CP/DP config sync enforces one matching value across the cluster before distribution. Null selects x-request-id.

echo_downstream.description: When true, this instance's resolved ID is added to ordinary responses, rejection responses, and successful H1 Upgrade/H2-H3 Extended CONNECT WebSocket handshakes. Null selects true.

inbound_policy.description: preserve keeps a well-formed inbound ID (at most 256 bytes matching [A-Za-z0-9._-]+) and replaces only missing or rejected values. generate always mints a fresh UUID v4 and overwrites any inbound value, so the backend header, downstream echo, canonical request_id log metadata, WebSocket handshake echo, and response_caching generated-value provenance all carry the gateway-owned ID. TCP/UDP sessions always generate. Null selects preserve.
